author: WPB5
summary: Alpha.1-era research audit (CNA 7a64362e) of input, devices and sensors, audio, media, networking, GamerServices, avatars and storage: per-API facts with line evidence, status tables and CNA-document contradictions. The service deep dives and module internals already carry nearly all of it at 009d40f5, including the stale parts' corrections (platform-service input, CNA_ENABLE_VIDEO, fixed Color/StorageContainer/Sensors defects). Residue added: how Microphone::Default is chosen at 009d40f5 (the synthetic 'Default Device' entry the audit describes is gone; host default first, real names).

sections.heading: 9. CROSS-CUTTING CONTRADICTIONS AND REPO-STATE FACTS
sections.note: A single-# part of the file, not a ## heading; recorded under its own title.

concepts.text: The audit's scale table (per-module production line counts and TEST-macro counts: input 522, audio 637, media 285, net 293, gamer-services 368, devices 462, devices-ext 50, storage 5, 6,171 in all) describes the alpha.1-era tree it was run against.
concepts.note: Counts of an earlier revision; the site publishes its own recomputed TARGET test totals (12,610 static GoogleTest definitions) and never per-module alpha.1 figures.

concepts.text: All input used to enter through one SDL_PollEvent site in Game::PollEvents, which fed every event to SdlInputBridge::ProcessEvent before the game loop's own switch.

target.evidence: modules/input/src (no SDL header); modules/platform/include/CNA/Platform/PlatformEvent.hpp

concepts.note: At 009d40f5 native input APIs live in cna_platform behind backend-neutral PlatformEvent values; the input module includes no SDL header. The events internals page states the current boundary.

concepts.text: Keyboard, Mouse, GamePad and TouchPanel GetState() are reads of state accumulated as events arrive, so two GetState() calls in one frame return identical snapshots (FNA re-queries SDL and could differ).

target.evidence: modules/input/src/Xna/Keyboard.cpp, Mouse.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: The input pipeline has no mutex or atomic by design; safety rests on pumping and reading both happening on the game-loop thread.

target.evidence: modules/input/src; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Keys has exactly 160 enumerators, numbered as the Windows virtual-key codes XNA uses.

target.evidence: modules/input/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Input/Keys.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: The SDL scancode-to-Keys table had 125 arms and the reverse table 126, so the two directions were not symmetric.
concepts.note: Counted in the alpha.1 SdlInputBridge.cpp; at 009d40f5 physical-key translation is owned by each platform backend (SDL3, X11 XKB, Wayland xkbcommon, Win32, terminal) and the bridge table no longer exists in that form.

concepts.text: KeyboardState stores pressed keys in an unordered_set, GetPressedKeys returns a vector, and CNAEXT adds a constructor from a key set and ToString.

target.evidence: modules/input/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Input/KeyboardState.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Mouse and touch positions are delivered in logical (render) coordinates, translated per window through the renderer, and Mouse::SetPosition applies the inverse transform on the window named by Mouse::WindowHandle or the focused one.

target.evidence: modules/input/src/Xna/Mouse.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.note: At 009d40f5 the lookup is a WindowId renderer registry rather than SDL_GetRenderer; the page states the current route.

concepts.text: Touch coordinates arrive normalized 0..1, are multiplied by the window's client size and then pass through the same logical transform as the mouse.

target.evidence: modules/input/src/Xna/Touch/TouchPanel.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: CNA's own input planning notes used the pre-rename NOXNA vocabulary, cited paths from before the modules/ split and a stale 524-test count.
concepts.note: Drift of CNA's internal Markdown at alpha.1 (NOXNA was renamed CNAEXT; paths moved under modules/); no technical claim for current users.

concepts.text: CNA_DEVICES defaults OFF, is emitted as a compile definition on the shared build-flags target, and gates everything in devices-ext but nothing in modules/devices: the Microsoft::Devices sensors and VibrateController exist in every build, while with the default the CNA::Devices types do not exist at all.

target.evidence: CMakeLists.txt (option CNA_DEVICES); modules/devices-ext/include (#ifdef CNA_DEVICES); already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: The CNA_DEVICES help string mentions sensors although sensors are not gated by it.
concepts.note: A wording nit of the alpha.1 option text; the site explains exactly what the option gates (host devices deep dive, option section), which is the useful fact.

concepts.text: SensorBase<T> is a header-only template that static_asserts its reading type, defaults TimeBetweenUpdates to 2 ms, and throws InvalidOperationException for CurrentValue on an unsupported sensor.

target.evidence: modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Sensors/SensorBase.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: TimeBetweenUpdates is a software throttle on a steady clock, not a hardware rate; the comparison casts elapsed time down to ticks to avoid a UBSan-found int64 overflow at TimeSpan::MaxValue.

target.evidence: SensorBase.hpp (ShouldAcceptUpdateAt); already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Accelerometer and Gyroscope are served by the platform's sensor service; web targets are refused by policy even where a browser sensor exists.
tokens: Web targets are refused by policy

target.evidence: modules/devices/src/Sensors/Accelerometer.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.note: Alpha.1 opened SDL sensors directly; at 009d40f5 the platform sensor service does.

concepts.text: Accelerometer divides SI m/s² by 9.80665 to report g, Gyroscope passes rad/s through unchanged, and reading timestamps are wall-clock at dispatch.

target.evidence: Accelerometer.cpp, Gyroscope.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Desktop sensor delivery has no polling thread: readings arrive through an event watch, so CurrentValueChanged fires on whichever thread delivers the platform event.

target.evidence: modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Sensors/Detail; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

target.evidence: modules/devices/src/Sensors/Compass.cpp, Motion.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: On Android, Compass and Motion use the NDK sensor API in C (ASensorManager, event queues, ALooper) without JNI, linked through cna_devices PUBLIC android log; the math headers are deliberately not Android-gated so they unit-test on Linux.

target.evidence: modules/devices/CMakeLists.txt; modules/devices/src/Sensors/Detail/AndroidSensorBridge.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Each Android sensor bridge owns one worker thread, and Motion owns six bridges (rotation vector, game rotation, gravity, linear acceleration, gyroscope, magnetic field).

target.evidence: modules/devices/src/Sensors/Detail/AndroidMotionBackend.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.note: The chapter record found the six-worker count stale at 009d40f5; the devices internals page states the current bridge model.

concepts.text: Compass heading math: a flat and an upright formula from the rotation quaternion, chosen by the gravity direction against cos 45°, with an invalid quaternion reported as 0° by policy.

target.evidence: modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Sensors/Detail/AndroidCompassMath.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: HeadingAccuracy maps High 5°, Medium 15°, Low 20° and Unreliable/NoContact 180°; Low is 20 so it cannot contradict WP7's calibrate rule.

target.evidence: AndroidCompassMath.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Compass TrueHeading deliberately equals MagneticHeading because no declination source exists.

target.evidence: modules/devices/src/Sensors/Detail/AndroidCompassBackend.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Motion attitude passes the rotation-vector components through as a normalized quaternion, and yaw, pitch and roll derive from its matrix (pitch = asin(clamp(-M32)), yaw = atan2(M31, M33), roll = atan2(M12, M22)).

target.evidence: modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Sensors/Detail/AndroidMotionMath.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: A CNAEXT landscape axis remap is on by default for accelerometer, gyroscope and Motion's vectors but not Attitude, because the remap is a reflection that no quaternion can express.

target.evidence: AndroidSensorOrientation.hpp; AndroidMotionMath.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Motion fuses the latest value of each source within a 500 ms window; timestamp-aligned fusion is deferred.

target.evidence: AndroidMotionBackend.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: VibrateController is real rumble, not a stub: durations are limited to WP7's zero to five seconds, strengths clamp to 0..1 with NaN treated as zero, and gamepads are excluded from its device choice so it never fights GamePad::SetVibration.

target.evidence: modules/devices/src/VibrateController.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: StartLeftRight plays two independent motors only on a device with a left/right effect and is otherwise emulated.

target.evidence: VibrateController.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: One process-wide mutex serialized SDL's sensor and haptic subsystem initialization, with lock order proven by an unused lock_guard parameter.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 no GetGlobalSdlSubsystemMutex exists under modules/; sensors and haptics acquire platform subsystems (PlatformSubsystem::Sensor / Haptic) through the platform layer.

concepts.text: DevicesShutdownCoordinator orders device shutdown before SDL_Quit so a function-local-static VibrateController cannot destroy after SDL freed the device (heap use-after-free), with an out-of-process ASan harness.

target.evidence: modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Detail/DevicesShutdownCoordinator.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.note: The chapter record found the alpha.1 ordering story stale; the devices internals page states the coordinator's current role.

concepts.text: SDL_INIT_CAMERA was never initialized anywhere, so CNA::Devices::Camera reported NotSupported unless the host initialized the camera subsystem itself.

target.evidence: modules/devices-ext/src/Camera.cpp (IPlatformCameraProvider from GetCurrentPlatform; capability camera)

concepts.note: At 009d40f5 the camera is reached through the platform's camera provider and capability flag, not a direct SDL subsystem; the host-devices deep dive describes the current route.

concepts.text: Camera frames are RGBA32 only; a device that negotiates another format is reported NotSupported, and frames reach a Texture2D.

target.evidence: modules/devices-ext/src/Camera.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Every other CNA::Devices class is a thin wrapper over a host service: Clipboard, DisplayInfo, Locale, MessageBox, FileDialog, SystemTray, PowerInfo, SystemInfo and UrlLauncher.

target.evidence: modules/devices-ext/src; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.note: Alpha.1 wrapped SDL directly; at 009d40f5 they go through platform services.

concepts.text: Gaps in the wrapper layer: dialogs are never parented and have no default or escape button, PowerInfo reads three independent snapshots, the tray icon has no image, and UrlLauncher does not validate.
concepts.note: Mixed status at 009d40f5: PowerInfo still reads GetPowerInfo once per property (modules/devices-ext/src/PowerInfo.cpp), and the dialog, tray and URL gaps are already issue candidates WP14-i038 and WP14-i040; the alpha.1 advisory platform checks and MessageBox IsSupported claims were found stale by the chapter record.

concepts.text: Dispose(bool) is public in the four sensor classes although SensorBase declares it protected; an external Dispose(false) marks the sensor disposed with no cleanup.

target.evidence: modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Sensors/Accelerometer.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.note: Still present at 009d40f5; the page states it as a scoped limitation and the chapter package recorded the issue candidate.

concepts.note: Still true at 009d40f5 (line counts unchanged); already recorded as issue candidate WP14-i034, not published as a page claim.

concepts.text: No hardware QA report has been filed: every Android sensor claim rests on source reading and host unit tests, and the compass math says its sign convention is unverified on hardware.

target.evidence: AndroidCompassMath.hpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: CNA::Input and CNA::Devices overlap by accident of two parallel workstreams: Clipboard and Power are true duplicates, CNA::Input::Sensors is a different poll-based API, InputDevices has no counterpart, and in a default build CNA::Input's clipboard and power are the only ones that exist.

target.evidence: modules/input/src/CnaExt; modules/devices-ext; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Per-suite test counts of the devices status table (SensorBase 26, Accelerometer 50, VibrateController 63 and so on).
concepts.note: Alpha.1 counts; the site does not publish per-suite counts.

concepts.text: CNA's device design documents contradicted the code (Compass/Motion called permanent stubs, LOW accuracy 45°, five bridges, an uninstrumented Android catch, a stale gtest filter and paths from before the modules/ split).
concepts.note: Drift inside CNA's own alpha.1 Markdown; the site states the code's behaviour directly.

concepts.text: CNA audio is SDL3_mixer (MIX_Mixer, MIX_Audio, MIX_Track), not FAudio and not a hand-written mixer.

target.evidence: modules/audio/CMakeLists.txt; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.note: True only for CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM=SDL3 at 009d40f5; ALSA uses CNA's own mixer (Backend/CnaMixer) and SDL2/NULL have none. The engine internals page states all four.

concepts.text: The SDL3 mixer device is always opened at a fixed S16, stereo, 44,100 Hz reference format rather than the device's native format, and the negotiated format is logged once.

target.evidence: modules/audio/src/Backend/Sdl3Mixer/MixerEngine.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Mixer creation is serialized by one mutex; a failed device creation balances the MIX_Init refcount before throwing, and DestroyMixer has no production caller, with a generation counter guarding stale tracks.

target.evidence: modules/audio/src/Backend/Sdl3Mixer; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: A permanently held extra SDL_INIT_AUDIO reference was pinned on first use so the mixer's own teardown could never zero the global refcount (an ASan-found SEGV).

target.evidence: modules/audio/src/Backend/Sdl3Mixer; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.note: The chapter record found the pin replaced by per-stream subsystem references at 009d40f5; the engine page describes the current lifetime.

concepts.text: File and stream SoundEffect loads go through the mixer's decoder with predecode enabled, so CNA decodes more than XNA's WAV-only SoundEffect.

target.evidence: modules/audio/src/Xna/SoundEffect.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: CNA's build narrows vendored SDL3_mixer: GME, XMP, mpg123, FluidSynth, Opus, libvorbisfile, Tremor, WavPack and libFLAC are off, leaving AIFF, WAVE, VOC, AU, drflac FLAC, dr_mp3 MP3, stb_vorbis Ogg and timidity MIDI; Opus, WavPack and AAC/WMA are not decodable.

target.evidence: cmake/ThirdPartySDL.cmake (SDLMIXER_* OFF); already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

target.evidence: modules/audio/src/Xna/SoundEffect.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: SoundEffect globals default to XNA's values (MasterVolume 1, DistanceScale 1, DopplerScale 1, SpeedOfSound 343.5); DistanceScale rejects values <= 0 and DopplerScale values < 0.

target.evidence: modules/audio/src/Xna/SoundEffect.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: MasterVolume is applied once as the mixer's master gain and never baked into per-track gain.

concepts.text: Pitch is 2^pitch fed to the track frequency ratio with a floor; the earlier linear formula agreed only at -1, 0 and +1 and was hidden because tests used pitch 0.

target.evidence: modules/audio/src/Xna/SoundEffectInstance.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Pan is a crossfeed matrix computed in a per-track callback (FNA's 2-to-2 coefficients), so hard panning does not silence the opposite speaker.

target.evidence: SoundEffectInstance.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Apply3D attenuation is FAudio's inverse law: full volume within DistanceScale and 1/normalized-distance beyond; pan projects onto the listener's real right axis Cross(Forward, Up).

target.evidence: SoundEffectInstance.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

concepts.text: Doppler follows F3DAudio's CalculateDoppler with its clamps and a final factor clamped to 0.5..4 (one octave down, two up).

target.evidence: SoundEffectInstance.cpp (std::clamp(dopplerFactor, 0.5f, 4.0f)); already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

target.evidence: SoundEffectInstance.cpp; already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5

target.evidence: SoundEffectInstance.cpp (INTERNAL_applyReverb); already stated on that page, which was checked at 009d40f5
